headline: Recommended National Grid underground conduit permit on Wheeler Street and a special permit for six units at 4 Day Court
summary: The committee held a public hearing on National Grid's petition to install underground conduit on Wheeler Street and voted to recommend approval with conditions. The committee also heard a presentation on Seaside Legal Solutions' application for a special permit at Day Court #4 to build six dwelling units and voted to recommend approval with conditions.
decisions: Recommended that the City Council permit National Grid to install underground facilities on Wheeler Street, with seven conditions, vote 3-0.

Recommended that the City Council grant Billiken Investments LLC a Special Permit (SCP2026-007) for Day Court #4 to construct six dwelling units and reduce the required distance between two principal buildings, with seven conditions, vote 3-0.

Planning & Development Committee Present: Chair, Councilor Jason Grow; Vice Chair, Councilor
Dylan Benson; Councilor Hannah Kimberley
Also Present: Legislative Aide, Lynds Jones
This meeting was conducted in person and remotely through ZOOM
Councilor Grow called the P&D meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.
Councilor Grow announced the names of the P&D Committee members in attendance.
1. PP#2026-005: Petition by National Grid to install underground facilities on Wheeler Street 
beginning at a point 194 feet South of the centerline of the intersection of Wheeler Street and 
Shore Hill Road and continuing approximately 2 feet in an East direction. National Grid is 
petitioning to install +/- 2 feet of underground conduit from pole 511 to property line of 115 
Wheeler Street, Gloucester, MA.
 Public Hearing Opened: 6:07 p.m.
 Speaking in Favor: Ismail Mikou, 44 River Street, Beverly stated that the customer would be
digging the trench and installing the conduit. He stated that the digging would take place on a grassy
area. He stated that there would be no traffic impact.
 Speaking in Opposition: None.
 Communications: Legislative Aide, Lynds Jones read the following memo from the DPW
Director, Michael Hale:
Planning & Development                           October 7, 2026                                 Page 2 of 13
 Questions from Councilors to Applicants/Staff: Councilor Benson asked for clarification
regarding the customer digging the trench. Ismail Mikou stated that the customer would have a
contracted electrician dig the trench and install the conduit and National Grid would run the cable. 
 Public Hearing Closed: 6:15 p.m.
Summary of Discussion: None.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Grow, seconded by Councilor Benson,
the Planning & Development Committee voted 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the City Council
permit Massachusetts Electric Company d/b/a National Grid, to locate poles, wires and fixtures, including
the necessary sustaining and protecting fixtures, along and across the public way, National Grid to install
underground facilities on Wheeler Street. Beginning at a point 194 feet South of the centerline of the
intersection of Wheeler Street and Shore Hill Road and continuing approximately 2 feet in an easternly
Planning & Development                           October 7, 2026                                 Page 3 of 13
direction. National Grid is petitioning to install +/- 2 feet of underground conduit from pole 511 to property
line of 115 Wheeler Street in Gloucester; MA - as shown on a plan included in the application dated July
8, 2026 – with the following conditions:  
1. Notification to the Department of Public Works 72 hours in advance of the proposed work. A 
construction schedule will be prepared by the applicant for review and acceptance by the 
Department of Public Works.
2. In the absence of a detailed construction plan, the Department of Public Works requests: all 
proposed conduits and appurtenances shall be placed so as to cause minimum conflict with 
existing underground utility services.
3. All excavations must be secured at all times.
4. All excavated trenches shall be patched flush with the surrounding asphalt using hot mix asphalt 
binder at the end of each work day, to minimize pedestrian hazards. Asphalt shall be applied in 
two lifts of 2-inches, totaling 4- inches.
5. Sidewalks must be restored with like material immediately after pole set.
6. Paving conditions must be approved by Public Works prior to issuance of road opening permit.
7. Any areas not paved be restored with grass and plantings as originally found.
2. SCP2026-007: The application of Seaside Legal Solutions, P.C. (Owner, Billiken Investments
LLC), Day Court #4, Map #219, Lot #155: GZO Sec. 2.3.1(7) “Conversion to or new multi-family
or apartment dwelling, four to six dwelling units,” and Sec. 3.2.2 fn (e) “No principal building
shall be closer to another principal building on the same site than the sum of their respective
heights; provided, however, that the City Council may by special permit authorize a reduction in
said distance upon a finding that such reduction is not detrimental because of view obstruction,
overshadowing, service access or visual crowding” in the R20 district. (cont. from July 22, 2026)

COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Grow, seconded by Councilor
Kimberly, the Planning & Development Committee voted 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the
City Council grant to Billiken Investments LLC, a Special Permit (SCP2026-007) for the property located
at Day Court #4, Assessors Map 219, Lot 155, R-20 district, pursuant to Gloucester Zoning Ordinance Sec.
2.3.1(7), “Conversion to or new multi-family or apartment dwelling, four to six dwelling units” to construct
six dwelling units and grant a special permit pursuant to GZO 3.2.2 fn(e) “Dimensional Requirements for
Multi-family Dwellings and Their Accessory Uses (other than signs)” to reduce the required distance
between two principal building as follows:  
Combined Proposed           Granted
Heights Distance Relief
Combined Heights of Buildings (feet): 51.2 20 31.2
The special permits are granted on the basis of plans and elevations dated October 21, 2025 (four plans for
4 Day Court), and submitted to the City Clerk on June 30, 2026, entitled “Existing Condition Plan,” “Survey
& Layout Plan,” “Grading and Drainage Plan,” “Construction Details Plan,” “Floor Plans,” “Elevations,”
“Roof Plan,” and “Improved Roadway Plan.” The Special Council Permit will have the following
conditions:
1. Prior to issuance of an occupancy permit for the first completed unit, Applicant must clear all trees
and brush between Homan’s Court and Day Court for the first 50’ of Day Court beginning at its
intersection with Essex Avenue. Applicant, and its successors and assigns, shall also have a
perpetual obligation to maintain a low-lying decorative vegetated border along the existing rock
border between Homan’s Court and Day Court within said 50’ in order to ensure visibility of
vehicles and pedestrians on both streets. Neither the initial clearing nor perpetual maintenance of
the vegetated border shall be done so as to reduce or impede the existing absorption of runoff within
such area nor destabilize the soil.
2. Prior to issuance of an occupancy permit for the first completed unit, Applicant must erect a 6’
wooden stockade fence or similar visual barrier made of natural materials (i.e. no vinyl) along the
southeasterly boundary of Day Court from a point beginning 50’ from Day Court’s intersection
with Essex Avenue and continuing for 100’. The Applicant, and its successors and assigns, shall
also have a perpetual obligation to maintain such visual barrier within said 100’.
3. All off-site improvements to Day Court must comply with all City of Gloucester drainage
regulations.
4. Any damage to Homan’s Court caused by construction activities on Day Court and/or Applicant’s
property shall be repaired at Applicant’s expense. 
5. Applicant shall offer to collect email addresses from interested neighbors and provide advance
notice of commencement of construction. 
6. The Applicant will construct a fence along the railway according to MBTA requirements.

7. The Applicant consult abutters regarding the final drainage plan to ensure proper drainage is
maintained in the future.
